audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for feeding sign, walking on sea/I am, bread from heaven discourse, flesh/blood hard saying, Spirit/life, Peter confession.

verses.restored: After these things Jesus went away to the other side of the sea of Galilee, the sea of Tiberias.

familiar.text: After these things Jesus went over the sea of Galilee, which is the sea of Tiberias.

modern.text: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee (that is, the Sea of Tiberias).

original.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀπῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Γαλιλαίας τῆς Τιβεριάδος.

verses.restored: A great crowd followed him, because they were beholding the signs he was doing on those who were weak.

familiar.text: And a great multitude followed him, because they saw his miracles which he did on them that were diseased.

modern.text: A large crowd followed Him because they saw the signs He was performing on the sick.

original.text: ⸂ἠκολούθει δὲ⸃ αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς, ὅτι ⸀ἐθεώρουν τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει ἐπὶ τῶν ἀσθενούντων.

verses.restored: Jesus went up into the mountain, and there he was sitting with his disciples.

familiar.text: And Jesus went up into a mountain, and there he sat with his disciples.

modern.text: Then Jesus went up on the mountain and sat down with His disciples.

original.text: ἀνῆλθεν δὲ εἰς τὸ ⸀ὄρος Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Now the Passover, the feast of the Judeans, was near.

familiar.text: And the passover, a feast of the Jews, was nigh.

modern.text: Now the Jewish Feast of the Passover was near.

original.text: ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς τὸ πάσχα, ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

verses.restored: Lifting up his eyes and beholding that a great crowd was coming to him, Jesus says to Philip, From where shall we buy bread so these may eat?

familiar.text: When Jesus then lifted up his eyes, and saw a great company come unto him, he saith unto Philip, Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat?

modern.text: When Jesus looked up and saw a large crowd coming toward Him, He said to Philip, “Where can we buy bread for these people to eat?”

original.text: ἐπάρας οὖν ⸂τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ καὶ θεασάμενος ὅτι πολὺς ὄχλος ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγει ⸀πρὸς Φίλιππον· Πόθεν ⸀ἀγοράσωμεν ἄρτους ἵνα φάγωσιν οὗτοι;

verses.restored: He said this testing him, for he himself knew what he was about to do.

familiar.text: And this he said to prove him: for he himself knew what he would do.

modern.text: But He was asking this to test him, for He knew what He was about to do.

original.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἔλεγεν πειράζων αὐτόν, αὐτὸς γὰρ ᾔδει τί ἔμελλεν ποιεῖν.

verses.restored: Philip answered him, Two hundred denarii of bread is not enough for them, so that each may receive a little.

familiar.text: Philip answered him, Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a little.

modern.text: Philip answered, “Two hundred denarii would not buy enough bread for each of them to have a small piece.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀αὐτῷ Φίλιππος· Διακοσίων δηναρίων ἄρτοι οὐκ ἀρκοῦσιν αὐτοῖς ἵνα ⸀ἕκαστος βραχύ ⸀τι λάβῃ.

verses.restored: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, says to him,

familiar.text: One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, saith unto him,

modern.text: One of His disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said to Him,

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ εἷς ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, Ἀνδρέας ὁ ἀδελφὸς Σίμωνος Πέτρου·

verses.restored: There is a little boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish; but what are these for so many?

familiar.text: There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?

modern.text: “Here is a boy with five barley loaves and two small fish. But what difference will these make among so many?”

original.text: Ἔστιν ⸀παιδάριον ὧδε ⸀ὃς ἔχει πέντε ἄρτους κριθίνους καὶ δύο ὀψάρια· ἀλλὰ ταῦτα τί ἐστιν εἰς τοσούτους;

verses.restored: Jesus said, Make the people recline. There was much grass in the place. So the men reclined, about five thousand in number.

familiar.text: And Jesus said, Make the men sit down. Now there was much grass in the place. So the men sat down, in number about five thousand.

modern.text: “Have the people sit down,” Jesus said. Now there was plenty of grass in that place, so the men sat down, about five thousand of them.

original.text: ⸀εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ποιήσατε τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἀναπεσεῖν. ἦν δὲ χόρτος πολὺς ἐν τῷ τόπῳ. ἀνέπεσαν οὖν οἱ ἄνδρες τὸν ἀριθμὸν ⸀ὡς πεντακισχίλιοι.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore took the loaves, and giving thanks, distributed to those reclining; likewise also from the fish, as much as they wanted.

familiar.text: And Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that were set down; and likewise of the fishes as much as they would.

modern.text: Then Jesus took the loaves and the fish, gave thanks, and distributed to those who were seated as much as they wanted.

original.text: ἔλαβεν ⸀οὖν τοὺς ἄρτους ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ⸀διέδωκεν τοῖς ἀνακειμένοις, ὁμοίως καὶ ἐκ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὅσον ἤθελον.

verses.restored: When they were filled, he says to his disciples, Gather the remaining broken pieces, so that nothing may be lost.

familiar.text: When they were filled, he said unto his disciples, Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.

modern.text: And when everyone was full, He said to His disciples, “Gather the pieces that are left over, so that nothing will be wasted.”

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἐνεπλήσθησαν λέγει τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Συναγάγετε τὰ περισσεύσαντα κλάσματα, ἵνα μή τι ἀπόληται.

verses.restored: So they gathered and filled twelve baskets of broken pieces from the five barley loaves, which remained over to those who had eaten.

familiar.text: Therefore they gathered them together, and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves, which remained over and above unto them that had eaten.

modern.text: So they collected them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves left over by those who had eaten.

original.text: συνήγαγον οὖν, καὶ ἐγέμισαν δώδεκα κοφίνους κλασμάτων ἐκ τῶν πέντε ἄρτων τῶν κριθίνων ἃ ⸀ἐπερίσσευσαν τοῖς βεβρωκόσιν.

verses.restored: Therefore the people, seeing the sign he did, were saying, This is truly the Prophet coming into the world.

familiar.text: Then those men, when they had seen the miracle that Jesus did, said, This is of a truth that prophet that should come into the world.

modern.text: When the people saw the sign that Jesus had performed, they began to say, “Truly this is the Prophet who is to come into the world.”

original.text: οἱ οὖν ἄνθρωποι ἰδόντες ⸂ὃ ἐποίησεν σημεῖον⸃ ⸀ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ προφήτης ὁ ἐρχόμενος εἰς τὸν κόσμον.

verses.restored: Jesus, knowing that they were about to come and seize him so they might make him king, withdrew again to the mountain by himself alone.

familiar.text: When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone.

modern.text: Then Jesus, realizing that they were about to come and make Him king by force, withdrew again to a mountain by Himself. Jesus Walks on Water (Matthew 14:22–33; Mark 6:45–52)

original.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν γνοὺς ὅτι μέλλουσιν ἔρχεσθαι καὶ ἁρπάζειν αὐτὸν ἵνα ⸀ποιήσωσιν βασιλέα ἀνεχώρησεν ⸀πάλιν εἰς τὸ ὄρος αὐτὸς μόνος.

verses.restored: When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.

familiar.text: And when even was now come, his disciples went down unto the sea,

modern.text: When evening came, His disciples went down to the sea,

original.text: Ὡς δὲ ὀψία ἐγένετο κατέβησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν,

verses.restored: Entering a boat, they were going across the sea to Capernaum. Darkness had already come, and Jesus had not yet come to them.

familiar.text: And entered into a ship, and went over the sea toward Capernaum. And it was now dark, and Jesus was not come to them.

modern.text: got into a boat, and started across the sea to Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet gone out to them.

original.text: καὶ ἐμβάντες ⸀εἰς πλοῖον ἤρχοντο πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς Καφαρναούμ. καὶ σκοτία ἤδη ἐγεγόνει καὶ ⸀οὔπω ἐληλύθει πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς,

verses.restored: The sea was being stirred because a strong wind was blowing.

familiar.text: And the sea arose by reason of a great wind that blew.

modern.text: A strong wind was blowing, and the sea grew agitated.

original.text: ἥ τε θάλασσα ἀνέμου μεγάλου πνέοντος ⸀διεγείρετο.

verses.restored: Having rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they behold Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were afraid.

familiar.text: So when they had rowed about five and twenty or thirty furlongs, they see Jesus walking on the sea, and drawing nigh unto the ship: and they were afraid.

modern.text: When they had rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus approaching the boat, walking on the sea—and they were terrified.

original.text: ἐληλακότες οὖν ὡς σταδίους εἴκοσι πέντε ἢ τριάκοντα θεωροῦσιν τὸν Ἰησοῦν περιπατοῦντα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐγγὺς τοῦ πλοίου γινόμενον, καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν.

verses.restored: But he says to them, I am; do not fear.

familiar.text: But he saith unto them, It is I; be not afraid.

modern.text: But Jesus spoke up: “It is I; do not be afraid.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.

verses.restored: Therefore they were willing to receive him into the boat, and immediately the boat came to the land to which they were going.

familiar.text: Then they willingly received him into the ship: and immediately the ship was at the land whither they went.

modern.text: Then they were willing to take Him into the boat, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading. Jesus the Bread of Life

original.text: ἤθελον οὖν λαβεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ εὐθέως ⸂ἐγένετο τὸ πλοῖον⸃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς εἰς ἣν ὑπῆγον.

verses.restored: The next day the crowd standing on the other side of the sea saw that there had been no other little boat there except one, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with his disciples, but his disciples went away alone.

familiar.text: The day following, when the people which stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was none other boat there, save that one whereinto his disciples were entered, and that Jesus went not with his disciples into the boat, but that his disciples were gone away alone;

modern.text: The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not boarded it with His disciples, but they had gone away alone.

original.text: Τῇ ἐπαύριον ὁ ὄχλος ὁ ἑστηκὼς πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης ⸀εἶδον ὅτι πλοιάριον ἄλλο οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖ εἰ μὴ ⸀ἕν, καὶ ὅτι οὐ συνεισῆλθεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ⸀πλοῖον ἀλλὰ μόνοι οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον·

verses.restored: Other boats came from Tiberias near the place where they ate the bread after the Lord gave thanks.

familiar.text: (Howbeit there came other boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place where they did eat bread, after that the Lord had given thanks:)

modern.text: However, some boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.

original.text: ⸀ἀλλὰ ἦλθεν ⸀πλοιάρια ἐκ Τιβεριάδος ἐγγὺς τοῦ τόπου ὅπου ἔφαγον τὸν ἄρτον εὐχαριστήσαντος τοῦ κυρίου.

verses.restored: When the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they entered the boats and went to Capernaum seeking Jesus.

familiar.text: When the people therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they also took shipping, and came to Capernaum, seeking for Jesus.

modern.text: So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.

original.text: ὅτε οὖν εἶδεν ὁ ὄχλος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκεῖ οὐδὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, ἐνέβησαν αὐτοὶ εἰς τὰ ⸀πλοιάρια καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ ζητοῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: Finding him across the sea, they said to him, Rabbi, when did you come here?

familiar.text: And when they had found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?

modern.text: When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, “Rabbi, when did You get here?”

original.text: Καὶ εὑρόντες αὐτὸν πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἶπον αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, πότε ὧδε γέγονας;

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, Amen, amen, I say to you: you seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate from the loaves and were filled.

familiar.text: Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled.

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ζητεῖτέ με οὐχ ὅτι εἴδετε σημεῖα ἀλλʼ ὅτι ἐφάγετε ἐκ τῶν ἄρτων καὶ ἐχορτάσθητε·

verses.restored: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food remaining into age-long life, which the Son of Humanity will give you; for on this one the Father, the Divine, has set his seal.

familiar.text: Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed.

modern.text: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”

original.text: ἐργάζεσθε μὴ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν ἀπολλυμένην ἀλλὰ τὴν βρῶσιν τὴν μένουσαν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἣν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὑμῖν δώσει, τοῦτον γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ἐσφράγισεν ὁ θεός.

verses.restored: They said to him, What shall we do, so that we may work the works of the Divine?

familiar.text: Then said they unto him, What shall we do, that we might work the works of God?

modern.text: Then they inquired, “What must we do to perform the works of God?”

original.text: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν· Τί ποιῶμεν ἵνα ἐργαζώμεθα τὰ ἔργα τοῦ θεοῦ;

verses.restored: Jesus answered and said to them, This is the work of the Divine: that you trust into the one whom that One sent.

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.

modern.text: Jesus replied, “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ⸀ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ ἔργον τοῦ θεοῦ ἵνα ⸀πιστεύητε εἰς ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος.

verses.restored: They said to him, What sign then do you do, so that we may see and trust you? What do you work?

familiar.text: They said therefore unto him, What sign shewest thou then, that we may see, and believe thee? what dost thou work?

modern.text: So they asked Him, “What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?

original.text: εἶπον οὖν αὐτῷ· Τί οὖν ποιεῖς σὺ σημεῖον, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμέν σοι; τί ἐργάζῃ;

verses.restored: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it has been written: He gave them bread from heaven to eat.

familiar.text: Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.

modern.text: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’ ”

original.text: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν τὸ μάννα ἔφαγον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, καθώς ἐστιν γεγραμμένον· Ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you: Moses has not given you the bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.

familiar.text: Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.

modern.text: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.

original.text: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ Μωϋσῆς ⸀δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἀλλʼ ὁ πατήρ μου δίδωσιν ὑμῖν τὸν ἄρτον ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ τὸν ἀληθινόν·

verses.restored: For the bread of the Divine is the one coming down from heaven and giving life to the world.

familiar.text: For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.

modern.text: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”

original.text: ὁ γὰρ ἄρτος τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ καταβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ζωὴν διδοὺς τῷ κόσμῳ.

verses.restored: They said to him, Lord, always give us this bread.

familiar.text: Then said they unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.

modern.text: “Sir,” they said, “give us this bread at all times.”

original.text: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτόν· Κύριε, πάντοτε δὸς ἡμῖν τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, I am the bread of life. The one coming to me will certainly not hunger, and the one trusting into me will certainly never thirst.

familiar.text: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.

original.text: ⸀Εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς· ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ πεινάσῃ, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ⸀ἐμὲ οὐ μὴ ⸀διψήσει πώποτε.

verses.restored: But I said to you that you have seen me and yet do not trust.

familiar.text: But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.

modern.text: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.

original.text: ἀλλʼ εἶπον ὑμῖν ὅτι καὶ ἑωράκατέ με καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε.

verses.restored: All that the Father gives me will come to me, and the one coming to me I will certainly not cast out,

familiar.text: All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.

modern.text: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.

original.text: πᾶν ὃ δίδωσίν μοι ὁ πατὴρ πρὸς ἐμὲ ἥξει, καὶ τὸν ἐρχόμενον πρός ⸀με οὐ μὴ ἐκβάλω ἔξω,

verses.restored: because I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of the One who sent me.

familiar.text: For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.

modern.text: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.

original.text: ὅτι καταβέβηκα ⸀ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οὐχ ἵνα ποιῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με·

verses.restored: This is the will of the One who sent me: that of all he has given me I should lose nothing, but raise it up on the last day.

familiar.text: And this is the Father’s will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.

modern.text: And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.

original.text: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός ⸀με ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκέν μοι μὴ ἀπολέσω ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἀλλὰ ἀναστήσω ⸀αὐτὸ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

verses.restored: For this is the will of my Father: that everyone beholding the Son and trusting into him may have age-long life, and I will raise that one up on the last day.

familiar.text: And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.

modern.text: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”

original.text: τοῦτο ⸀γάρ ἐστιν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ ⸂πατρός μου⸃ ἵνα πᾶς ὁ θεωρῶν τὸν υἱὸν καὶ πιστεύων εἰς αὐτὸν ἔχῃ ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ⸀ἐγὼ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

verses.restored: Therefore the Judeans were grumbling about him because he said, I am the bread that came down from heaven.

familiar.text: The Jews then murmured at him, because he said, I am the bread which came down from heaven.

modern.text: At this, the Jews began to grumble about Jesus because He had said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”

original.text: Ἐγόγγυζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ καταβὰς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ,

verses.restored: They were saying, Is this not Jesus son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How now does he say, I have come down from heaven?

familiar.text: And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?

modern.text: They were asking, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven?’”

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγον· ⸀Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ υἱὸς Ἰωσήφ, οὗ ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα; πῶς ⸀νῦν ⸀λέγει ὅτι Ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβέβηκα;

verses.restored: Jesus answered and said to them, Do not grumble with one another.

familiar.text: Jesus therefore answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.

modern.text: “Stop grumbling among yourselves,” Jesus replied.

original.text: ⸀ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Μὴ γογγύζετε μετʼ ἀλλήλων.

verses.restored: No one is able to come to me unless the Father who sent me draws that one, and I will raise that one up on the last day.

familiar.text: No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.

modern.text: “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.

original.text: οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός ⸀με ἐὰν μὴ ὁ πατὴρ ὁ πέμψας με ἑλκύσῃ αὐτόν, κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

verses.restored: It has been written in the Prophets: And they will all be taught by the Divine. Everyone who hears from the Father and learns comes to me.

familiar.text: It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me.

modern.text: It is written in the Prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me—

original.text: ἔστιν γεγραμμένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις· Καὶ ἔσονται πάντες διδακτοὶ θεοῦ· ⸀πᾶς ὁ ⸀ἀκούσας παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ μαθὼν ἔρχεται πρὸς ⸀ἐμέ.

verses.restored: Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one being from the Divine; this one has seen the Father.

familiar.text: Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father.

modern.text: not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father.

original.text: οὐχ ὅτι τὸν πατέρα ⸂ἑώρακέν τις⸃ εἰ μὴ ὁ ὢν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗτος ἑώρακεν τὸν πατέρα.

verses.restored: Amen, amen, I say to you: the one trusting has age-long life.

familiar.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life.

modern.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.

original.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ ⸀πιστεύων ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

verses.restored: I am the bread of life.

familiar.text: I am that bread of life.

modern.text: I am the bread of life.

original.text: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς·

verses.restored: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.

familiar.text: Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead.

modern.text: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.

original.text: οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἔφαγον ⸂ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τὸ μάννα⸃ καὶ ἀπέθανον·

verses.restored: This is the bread coming down from heaven, so that one may eat from it and not die.

familiar.text: This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.

modern.text: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.

original.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνων ἵνα τις ἐξ αὐτοῦ φάγῃ καὶ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·

verses.restored: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats from this bread, that one will live into the age; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my embodied life.

familiar.text: I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.

modern.text: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.”

original.text: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς· ἐάν τις φάγῃ ἐκ τούτου τοῦ ἄρτου ⸀ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ ὁ ἄρτος δὲ ὃν ἐγὼ δώσω ἡ σάρξ μού ⸀ἐστιν ὑπὲρ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου ζωῆς.

verses.restored: Therefore the Judeans were disputing with one another, saying, How is this one able to give us his embodied life to eat?

familiar.text: The Jews therefore strove among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?

modern.text: At this, the Jews began to argue among themselves, “How can this man give us His flesh to eat?”

original.text: Ἐμάχοντο οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες· Πῶς δύναται οὗτος ἡμῖν δοῦναι τὴν σάρκα ⸀αὐτοῦ φαγεῖν;

verses.restored: Jesus therefore said to them, Amen, amen, I say to you: unless you eat the embodied life of the Son of Humanity and drink his blood, you do not have life in yourselves.

familiar.text: Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you.

modern.text: So Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.

original.text: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ φάγητε τὴν σάρκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πίητε αὐτοῦ τὸ αἷμα, οὐκ ἔχετε ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.

verses.restored: The one eating my embodied life and drinking my blood has age-long life, and I will raise that one up on the last day.

familiar.text: Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

modern.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.

original.text: ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

verses.restored: For my embodied life is true food, and my blood is true drink.

familiar.text: For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.

modern.text: For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.

original.text: ἡ γὰρ σάρξ μου ⸀ἀληθής ἐστι βρῶσις, καὶ τὸ αἷμά μου ⸁ἀληθής ἐστι πόσις.

verses.restored: The one eating my embodied life and drinking my blood remains in me, and I in that one.

familiar.text: He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him.

modern.text: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.

original.text: ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μένει κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Just as the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so also the one eating me will live because of me.

familiar.text: As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me.

modern.text: Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.

original.text: καθὼς ἀπέστειλέν με ὁ ζῶν πατὴρ κἀγὼ ζῶ διὰ τὸν πατέρα, καὶ ὁ τρώγων με κἀκεῖνος ⸀ζήσει διʼ ἐμέ.

verses.restored: This is the bread that came down from heaven, not as the fathers ate and died; the one eating this bread will live into the age.

familiar.text: This is that bread which came down from heaven: not as your fathers did eat manna, and are dead: he that eateth of this bread shall live for ever.

modern.text: This is the bread that came down from heaven. Unlike your fathers, who ate the manna and died, the one who eats this bread will live forever.” Many Disciples Turn Back (Matthew 8:18–22; Luke 9:57–62; Luke 14:25–33)

original.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ⸀ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς, οὐ καθὼς ἔφαγον οἱ ⸀πατέρες καὶ ἀπέθανον· ὁ τρώγων τοῦτον τὸν ἄρτον ⸀ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

verses.restored: He said these things teaching in a synagogue in Capernaum.

familiar.text: These things said he in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.

modern.text: Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.

original.text: ταῦτα εἶπεν ἐν συναγωγῇ διδάσκων ἐν Καφαρναούμ.

verses.restored: Therefore many of his disciples, hearing, said, This word is hard; who is able to hear it?

familiar.text: Many therefore of his disciples, when they had heard this, said, This is an hard saying; who can hear it?

modern.text: On hearing it, many of His disciples said, “This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?”

original.text: Πολλοὶ οὖν ἀκούσαντες ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ εἶπαν· Σκληρός ἐστιν ⸂ὁ λόγος οὗτος⸃· τίς δύναται αὐτοῦ ἀκούειν;

verses.restored: Jesus, knowing in himself that his disciples were grumbling about this, said to them, Does this cause you to stumble?

familiar.text: When Jesus knew in himself that his disciples murmured at it, he said unto them, Doth this offend you?

modern.text: Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching, Jesus asked them, “Does this offend you?

original.text: εἰδὼς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὅτι γογγύζουσιν περὶ τούτου οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο ὑμᾶς σκανδαλίζει;

verses.restored: Then what if you behold the Son of Humanity ascending where he was before?

familiar.text: What and if ye shall see the Son of man ascend up where he was before?

modern.text: Then what will happen if you see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?

original.text: ἐὰν οὖν θεωρῆτε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀναβαίνοντα ὅπου ἦν τὸ πρότερον;

verses.restored: The Spirit is the one making alive; ordinary human nature profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are Spirit and are life.

familiar.text: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.

modern.text: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.

original.text: τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν τὸ ζῳοποιοῦν, ἡ σὰρξ οὐκ ὠφελεῖ οὐδέν· τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ ⸀λελάληκα ὑμῖν πνεῦμά ἐστιν καὶ ζωή ἐστιν.

verses.restored: But there are some among you who do not trust. For Jesus knew from the beginning who those were who did not trust, and who was the one handing him over.

familiar.text: But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who should betray him.

modern.text: However, there are some of you who do not believe.” (For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.)

original.text: ἀλλὰ εἰσὶν ἐξ ὑμῶν τινες οἳ οὐ πιστεύουσιν. ᾔδει γὰρ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τίνες εἰσὶν οἱ μὴ πιστεύοντες καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ παραδώσων αὐτόν.

verses.restored: He was saying, Because of this I have said to you that no one is able to come to me unless it has been given to that one from the Father.

familiar.text: And he said, Therefore said I unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it were given unto him of my Father.

modern.text: Then Jesus said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him.”

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν· Διὰ τοῦτο εἴρηκα ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἐὰν μὴ ᾖ δεδομένον αὐτῷ ἐκ τοῦ ⸀πατρός.

verses.restored: From this, many of his disciples went away to the things behind and no longer walked with him.

familiar.text: From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.

modern.text: From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him. Peter’s Confession of Faith (Matthew 16:13–20; Mark 8:27–30; Luke 9:18–20)

original.text: Ἐκ τούτου πολλοὶ ⸀ἐκ ⸂τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀπῆλθον⸃ εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω καὶ οὐκέτι μετʼ αὐτοῦ περιεπάτουν.

verses.restored: Therefore Jesus said to the twelve, Do you also want to go away?

familiar.text: Then said Jesus unto the twelve, Will ye also go away?

modern.text: So Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you want to leave too?”

original.text: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς δώδεκα· Μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς θέλετε ὑπάγειν;

verses.restored: Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? You have words of age-long life.

familiar.text: Then Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

modern.text: Simon Peter replied, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.

original.text: ⸀ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ Σίμων Πέτρος· Κύριε, πρὸς τίνα ἀπελευσόμεθα; ῥήματα ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἔχεις,

verses.restored: And we have trusted and have known that you are the Holy One of the Divine.

familiar.text: And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.

modern.text: We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God. ”

original.text: καὶ ἡμεῖς πεπιστεύκαμεν καὶ ἐγνώκαμεν ὅτι σὺ εἶ ὁ ⸀ἅγιος τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, Did I not choose you, the twelve? Yet one of you is adversarial.

familiar.text: Jesus answered them, Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?

modern.text: Jesus answered them, “Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐκ ἐγὼ ὑμᾶς τοὺς δώδεκα ἐξελεξάμην; καὶ ἐξ ὑμῶν εἷς διάβολός ἐστιν.

verses.restored: He was speaking of Judas son of Simon Iscariot, for this one, one of the twelve, was about to hand him over.

familiar.text: He spake of Judas Iscariot the son of Simon: for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve.

modern.text: He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.

original.text: ἔλεγεν δὲ τὸν Ἰούδαν Σίμωνος ⸀Ἰσκαριώτου· οὗτος γὰρ ἔμελλεν ⸂παραδιδόναι αὐτόν⸃, ⸀εἷς ἐκ τῶν δώδεκα.
